question.text: The concept of 'TAX NEUTRALITY' in fund structuring means:

answer.text: The fund pays zero tax in India
Investors in the fund should not be subject to higher aggregate taxes than if they had invested directly in the underlying assets
All investors pay the same effective tax rate regardless of residency
The fund can elect its own tax rate annually

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax neutrality = investing through the fund should not put an investor in a WORSE tax position than direct investing. The fund should be a conduit that doesn't ADD tax drag. Achieving perfect neutrality is difficult when the fund is taxed at entity level (as in Cat III's fund-level MMR taxation) but is the design aspiration. The Trap: Options A, C, D are fabrications. Tax neutrality does NOT mean zero tax or flat rate for all — it means no worse than direct investing. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D all test this definition. Real test of neutrality is especially relevant for Cat III where fund-level MMR is not pass-through like Cat I/II's Section 115UB. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III's fund-level MMR (around 42.7% surcharge-inclusive for AOPs) means perfect neutrality is impossible for low-tax-rate investors. Disclose this in PPM and never promise tax-neutrality to investors.
